solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Petty Sergeant-Major everybody paid attention to

parts.note: everybody means all
to have minded something is to have paid attention to it

explanation.surface: A complaint that a petty sergeant-major is the one everybody listened to.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone petty fusses over trifles, which is what a narrow, small-minded outlook does.

clue.text: Cat ascending over river remains air-bound!

indicators.note: the reversed cat word sits over the river, wrapping round it here
in a down clue, going upwards means the word for cat is read from bottom to top

parts.note: puss is an affectionate word for a cat
the Tay is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A cat climbing above a river seems to be floating in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'ascending' reads upwards; 'over' here means wrapped around, giving S-TAY-SUP. The exclamation mark plays on a cat stranded up high.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that remains aloft without coming down is said to keep itself up in the air.

clue.text: Revolutionary army with course of action, making assault

indicators.note: revolving the letters means the abbreviation for the army is turned round

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
a tack is a course of action or approach, from sailing

explanation.surface: A revolutionary army picks its course of action and launches an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault is a violent onslaught, the same as an offensive strike on an enemy.

clue.text: Later luck's out — one gets dull

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone whose luck has run out ends up a dull figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking shine or energy, so dull and uninspiring in performance or appearance.

clue.text: I am, before noon, a man of prayer

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
a.m. is ante meridiem, the hours before noon

explanation.surface: A man introduces himself, before midday, as someone who leads prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: An imam leads the prayers in a mosque, so is a Muslim prayer leader.

clue.text: Emerges from railway journey inert, sad, wretched

indicators.note: wretched suggests a sorry, wrecked state, so the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A passenger stepping off a train feels listless, sad and miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: To get off a train at the end of a rail trip is to leave the carriage at a station.

clue.text: Compound — one farm animal brought inside died unfortunately

indicators.note: these words place one piece within the rearranged letters
unfortunately suggests things going wrong, so the letters are put into a different order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A farm animal taken indoors died, poisoned by some chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the death word to DIDE, and 'brought inside' places the numeral and the beast after its first D. 'Compound' is a chemical, not an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical compound with two oxygen atoms per molecule, such as carbon's familiar gas.

clue.text: Talk about bozo ultimately in charge being disorganised

indicators.note: about places the talk word around a single letter

parts.note: a chat is informal talk

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Gossip that a clown has finally been put in charge, and everything is in disarray.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos is utter disorder, so something in a state of chaos is thoroughly disorganised.

clue.text: Comic lad playing with pet becoming confused

indicators.note: playing suggests fooling about, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A funny boy messing about with his pet ends up muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Confused here means intricate and tangled, hard to follow or unravel.

clue.text: Place for early Christians moving to China

indicators.note: moving signals the letters shift into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Early believers relocating to China.
explanation.walkthrough: Antioch, in present-day Turkey, is where Jesus's followers were first called Christians.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Syrian city was an important centre of the first-century church.

clue.text: Capital offence? Others hang, I will get free

indicators.note: letters set free are loosed from their order and reassembled

explanation.surface: A condemned prisoner boasts that others will hang while he goes free.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'capital' means punishable by death rather than urban.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason against the sovereign was historically punishable by death, making it a capital crime.

clue.text: Party character in Athens almost ill with beer

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for ill is cut off

parts.note: sick means ill
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A Greek visitor, feeling a bit off, carries on with beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A musicale is a social gathering featuring a musical performance, a kind of soirée.

clue.text: Very hot support Conservative's lost

indicators.note: lost tells us one letter has gone missing from the support word

parts.note: backing is support
C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: A political note: support for the Tories has evaporated in a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: Baking is a colloquial intensifier for scorching weather, as in a baking day.

clue.text: Is series of lectures spanning two days treated formally?

indicators.note: the two-day abbreviation stretches across and encloses the rest

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day, so two of them make DD
a course is a series of lectures

explanation.surface: Is a lecture course that runs over two days handled with proper formality?
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse on a subject is to speak or write about it at length and formally.

clue.text: Drinks bringing endless moral failure?

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a lapse is a moral slip or failure

explanation.surface: Does drinking lead to never-ending moral decline?
explanation.definitionFit: An animal drinks by lapping, so a cat laps its milk.

clue.text: Task in which worker keeps messing about

indicators.note: keeps means the worker holds the other letters within

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: about suggests moving around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A job during which an employee keeps fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: An assignment is a piece of work allocated to someone, a set job.

clue.text: Dwarf on isle, one with special role in film

definitions.text: one with special role in film

parts.note: to stunt growth is to dwarf it
Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A dwarf living on an island lands a special part in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A stuntman performs the dangerous action scenes in a film in place of an actor.

clue.text: Put a check on board's decree

parts.note: a counter is a board or surface over which business is done
an act is a decree or statute

explanation.surface: A board's ruling that puts a restraint on something.
explanation.definitionFit: To counteract is to neutralise or offset, so to hold something in check.

clue.text: Not like 'cheesy' photographs?

parts.note: photographers make subjects say 'cheese' for posed shots, so candid snaps are unlike them

explanation.surface: A remark distinguishing natural pictures from cheesy grinning ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural shot taken without arranging the subject is candid rather than staged.

clue.text: Sword carried by the peer

indicators.note: carried by tells us the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A lord bears a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword with a stiff blade.

clue.text: One receiving promise to be quietly guided — gosh!

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly
led means guided
gee is an exclamation of surprise like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at being quietly guided.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, the person to whom something is pledged, the recipient of a pledge or pawn.

clue.text: The French gent is given a reprieve

parts.note: le is the French for the
a toff is an upper-class gent

explanation.surface: A French gentleman escapes punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: To be excused a punishment is to be spared it, pardoned at the last moment.

clue.text: Securing bit of metal into label

indicators.note: into places the metal piece inside the label

parts.note: a tag is a label
a pin is a small piece of metal

explanation.surface: Fixing a piece of metal onto a label.
explanation.definitionFit: Taping something is fastening it down with adhesive strip, so securing it.

clue.text: Game at Millwall's ground starts to erupt so suddenly — loutish behaviour

parts.note: RU is rugby union
The Den is the home stadium of Millwall, a London football club

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out suddenly at a London football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudeness is ill-mannered, boorish conduct of the kind associated with louts.

clue.text: Advance payment comes with a loveless communication

indicators.note: love is zero, the letter O in tennis, so loveless removes it

parts.note: a note is a short written communication

explanation.surface: A down payment arrives with a cold, unfriendly letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is a stake put up before the deal.

clue.text: Fellow without hesitation to go round street — as collector

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the fellow surrounds the rest

parts.note: Dan is a short form of a man's name, used here for any fellow

indicators.note: the hesitation word goes around the street abbreviation

parts.note: um is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: A man going round a street, without pausing, as a collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking. A UK dustman collects household rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A dustman collects refuse from bins on his round, a rubbish collector.

clue.text: Hard work at home, energy limited? Drink needed

indicators.note: the energy letter is limited, hemmed in, by the hard-work word

parts.note: a slog is hard work
in means at home

explanation.surface: After hard work at home with energy running low, a drink is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: A liqueur made by steeping blackthorn fruit in gin, so an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Author in deal arranged with editor turned enemy

indicators.note: arranged signals the letters are put into a new order
turned means the editor abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: A writer in a book deal falls out with the editor, who becomes an enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes DANIEL from IN DEAL; 'turned' makes DE from ED.
explanation.definitionFit: The English writer of Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.
